software_engineering_governance_definiti.description: SEGD (Software Engineering Governance Definition) is an additive domain governance definition for software engineering execution, validation, change control, artifact identity, deployment-result traceability, repair, rollback, rerun, and engineering lineage. SEGD does not replace parent reasoning governance, parent behavior governance, or external orchestration; it defines software-engineering-specific domain delta only.

domain_scope.scope_statement: govern software engineering execution and validation from development objective through requirements, specification, repository-bound changes, tests, build, artifact identity, deployment-result capture, repair, rollback, rerun, and lineage records

domain_responsibility_boundary.authority_limit: SEGD may report engineering readiness, evidence gaps, invalidation conditions, and authority-reference gaps; it does not grant approval, assign accountability, delegate authority, or route domains.

abstraction_and_context_policy.purpose: keep SEGD rules abstract enough for software engineering across languages, repositories, tools, platforms, and deployment environments while allowing context-local specificity when needed to preserve engineering meaning

role_complete_separation.principle: SEGD must keep software engineering execution and validation separate from consulting, architecture ownership, generic agentic execution, continuous operations, authority ownership, project coordination, artifact publication quality, external orchestration, and parent governance.

separation_targets.domain_definition: software engineering execution, validation, artifact identity, repair origins, rerun scope, and lineage
separation_targets.inherited_governance: parent reasoning and behavior governance referenced as authoritative context and not reexpanded
separation_targets.external_orchestration: routing, registry, domain priority, and activation orchestration remain external
separation_targets.sibling_reference: sibling domains may be referenced for handoff conditions but their rules are not absorbed
separation_targets.governed_target: repository-bound software engineering object, process, change, artifact, state, or claim
separation_targets.records: domain-local records for engineering process and evaluation incident repair only
separation_targets.metadata: identity, compatibility, authorship, license, and repository information only

cross_domain_interference_policy.purpose: prevent SEGD from absorbing neighboring domains while preserving useful handoff condition findings

declared_sibling_boundaries.dcagd: development consulting, technical option comparison, design direction discussion, feasibility, and rough effort remain outside SEGD
declared_sibling_boundaries.aiagd: AI system architecture object and model retrieval memory tool agent placement remain outside SEGD
declared_sibling_boundaries.aagd: generic agentic execution, tool call, checkpoint, handoff, retry, and side effect governance remain outside SEGD
declared_sibling_boundaries.omrgd: continuous operations, maintenance, reliability improvement, and incident response lifecycle remain outside SEGD
declared_sibling_boundaries.daagd: approval ownership, accountability, delegation, and authority decision remain outside SEGD
declared_sibling_boundaries.aisgd: AI-mediated security risk remains outside SEGD
declared_sibling_boundaries.pmogd: work item, owner, deadline, blocker, milestone, and delivery coordination remain outside SEGD
declared_sibling_boundaries.acrgd: artifact structure, document quality, and publication-output governance remain outside SEGD

development_objective_intake.purpose: bind the originating development request to a concrete software engineering objective without converting consultation, authority, or operations ownership into SEGD responsibility

requirement_and_acceptance_criteria_bind.purpose: bind requirements and acceptance criteria that the engineering change will claim to satisfy

specification_binding.purpose: connect requirements to a concrete specification or explicitly mark specification gaps

engineering_scope_and_impact_analysis.purpose: identify files, components, interfaces, dependencies, tests, build targets, and deployment surfaces affected by the change

design_trace_binding.purpose: bind design decisions to implementation effects without absorbing development consulting or AI architecture governance

repository_and_base_revision_binding.purpose: bind repository, branch, base revision, and change boundary before modifying software artifacts

implementation_plan.purpose: define the implementation approach and validation plan for the selected engineering change without taking over technical option consulting

source_config_dependency_change.purpose: track source code, configuration, dependency, and migration changes within the bound scope

local_static_validation.purpose: capture static, local, or pre-test validation evidence and prevent local checks from being overclaimed

unit_test_validation.purpose: map unit tests to requirements, specifications, changed components, and regression claims

integration_and_regression_validation.purpose: validate integration and regression scope without treating narrower evidence as broader system correctness

security_dependency_and_supply_chain_che.purpose: check software security engineering concerns such as secrets, dependency integrity, branch protection, and artifact provenance without absorbing AI-mediated security governance

review_and_authority_reference_check.purpose: record engineering review state and authority references without deciding approval ownership or delegation authority

build_and_artifact_identity.purpose: bind build results, build environment, and artifact identity to the validated change

deployment_readiness_check.purpose: check readiness for deployment as an engineering run state without claiming continuous operational ownership

deployment_result_capture.purpose: capture the immediate deployment result and prevent deployment completion from being overclaimed as operational success

incident_or_failure_signal_capture.purpose: capture incident or failure signals linked to the engineering change without taking ownership of continuous incident response lifecycle

repair_or_rollback_origin_selection.purpose: select the earliest valid engineering repair or rollback origin and preserve prior state

retest_rebuild_redeploy_rerun.purpose: execute or record the necessary validation, build, deployment, and rerun scope after repair or rollback

audit_and_status_emission.purpose: emit domain-local status, evidence gaps, invalidation conditions, repair state, and handoff condition findings without taking external routing or approval authority

evaluation_policy.enabled_reason: software engineering readiness and success claims require explicit evidence, severity, and invalidation handling across artifacts, tests, builds, deployments, repair, and lineage

repair.purpose: define software-engineering-specific repair origins, affected scopes, rollback or rerun directions, and post-repair validation without replacing the parent repair cycle

software_engineering_process_record.purpose: record what software engineering change was attempted, why, under which requirement, specification, design trace, repository state, validation evidence, build artifact, deployment result, and repair or rerun state

evaluation_incident_and_repair_record.schema_name: SEGD Evaluation, Incident, and Repair Record
evaluation_incident_and_repair_record.purpose: record how an engineering change, build, deployment, or runtime-linked signal was evaluated, where it failed, what was invalidated, how repair, rollback, or rerun was scoped, and which status outputs or handoff conditions were emitted
